gloss: highlight, best scene, moment to shine

definitions.explanation: The most impressive or exciting part of a performance, event, game, or situation. Originally a theater term for the climactic scene, now used broadly for any moment that grabs attention.

examples.japanese: ここが{一番|いちばん}の{見|み}せ{場|ば}だ。
{後半|こうはん}に{見|み}せ{場|ば}を{作|つく}って{逆転|ぎゃくてん}した。
examples.english: They created a highlight in the second half and made a comeback.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{派手|はで}なアクションの{見|み}せ{場|ば}が{多|おお}く、{最後|さいご}まで{飽|あ}きずに{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: This movie has many flashy action highlights, so you can enjoy it without getting bored until the end.

notes:
USAGE:
{見|み}せ{場|ば} comes from {見|み}せる (to show) + {場|ば} (scene, place). Originally a theatrical term for the climactic or most dramatically effective scene, it is now widely used for sports, presentations, performances, and everyday situations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見|み}せ{場|ば}を{作|つく}る (create a highlight, make a moment to shine)
- {見|み}せ{場|ば}がない (no highlight, no moment to shine)
- {最大|さいだい}の{見|み}せ{場|ば} (the biggest highlight)
- {見|み}せ{場|ば}たっぷり (full of highlights)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ハイライト: highlight (loanword, used similarly but more casual)
- {見|み}どころ: highlight, point of interest (things worth seeing, often for tourism or events)
- クライマックス: climax (loanword, specifically the peak of dramatic tension)
